why_realistic: The demand lane already shipped one max() written as protection that the data always approached from below: the demand freshness floor, which score.py's own docstring now records as a flat penalty of roughly 40 percent rather than the protection it read as. Supply ages arrive overwhelmingly from below a collection interval, so flooring age at the cadence pins every same-day item to one freshness value, protective in wording and a flat penalty on the newest signals in fact.

# Collection runs in batches, so an age below one collection interval is timestamp noise
    # (a backfilled or republished item claiming the current hour) rather than a genuinely
    # newer signal. Floor the age at the cadence before decay, so the freshest band is not
    # decided by a difference the collector cannot actually measure.
    cadence_h = float(sc.get("collection_cadence_h", 6.0))
    fr = freshness(max(cadence_h, float(age_h)), sc.get("freshness_half_life_h", 72),
                   sc.get("freshness_gravity", 1.8))
oracle:
"""Supply freshness must keep resolving INSIDE the same-day band.

Supply is the hotness column and almost all of its traffic is hours old, so the ordering that
actually decides the daily feed is the ordering among same-day items. A floor applied to age before
decay collapses that whole band onto one value: every item younger than the floor scores identically,
the newest signal gains nothing over a half-day-old one, and the flattened value is strictly worse
than the one the freshest item had earned. Monotonicity in the large survives, which is why a suite
that only compares one hour against ten days stays green, so this asserts the STRICT ordering in the
small, which is where supply ranking actually happens.
"""
import score
from lib import load_config

DIMS = ("track_fit", "timing", "feasibility", "competition", "executability")


def _at(age_h):
    cfg = load_config()
    bd = {d: 75.0 for d in DIMS}
    return score.score_opportunity(bd, 3, age_h, None, 1.0, cfg, "emerging", side="supply")


def test_same_day_ages_are_still_ordered_strictly():
    a, b, c = _at(0.5)["freshness"], _at(3.0)["freshness"], _at(9.0)["freshness"]
    assert a > b > c, "same-day freshness collapsed: 0.5h=%s 3h=%s 9h=%s" % (a, b, c)


def test_the_newest_item_outscores_a_few_hours_old_one():
    assert _at(0.5)["final_score"] > _at(3.0)["final_score"]
    assert _at(3.0)["final_score"] > _at(9.0)["final_score"]


def test_a_brand_new_item_still_reaches_the_top_of_the_freshness_scale():
    """Over-rejection guard: a flat penalty on the freshest band shows up as a brand new item that
    can no longer reach the top of the range."""
    assert _at(0.0)["freshness"] > 0.98
